en: Hello {contact}, we have a bundle offer for your shop. Tell us your tier ({tier}) and we will send the prices.
Hello {contact}, the minimum order for your tier ({tier}) is now {min_order}. Please tell us if this causes a problem.
Hello, we want to review our rates for {service}, zone {zone}. Our rates were last checked on {checked}. Please send the current rate card.
Hello, please explain the fuel surcharge of {fuel_pct} and the minimum charge of {min_charge} on {service}, zone {zone}.
Team member: promo prices go live
Hello, promo prices go live on {starts} for {sku} on {channel}: {promo_price}. The promotion ends on {ends}. Please change prices and tags.
Hello, please change the price tag of {sku} on the market stall to {new_price} from {date}.
Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

Unit cost ex-works is {col:products.unit_cost} and landed cost is {col:products.landed_cost}, of which freight and duty are {col:products.freight_duty}. The parcel weight is {col:products.weight_g} g.

Prices before sales tax: web shop {col:products.price_web}, Marketplace A {col:products.price_a}, Marketplace B {col:products.price_b}, social shop {col:products.price_social}, wholesale {col:products.price_wholesale}.

Margins after fees, packaging, shipping and returns: web shop {col:products.m_web}, Marketplace A {col:products.m_a}, Marketplace B {col:products.m_b}, social shop {col:products.m_social}, wholesale {col:products.m_ws}. Channels under the floor: {col:products.n_under}.
Price list of one product on every channel
Price list of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Prices are before sales tax.

Own web shop {col:products.price_web}; Marketplace A {col:products.price_a}; Marketplace B {col:products.price_b}; social shop {col:products.price_social}; wholesale and markets {col:products.price_wholesale}.
The wholesale price is {col:products.ws_pct} of the web price. Markup of the web price over landed cost is {col:products.markup_web}.
Prices change only through a signed price change sheet and the change is entered in the price history.
Wholesale price list for a customer
Wholesale price terms of {set:shop} for {col:customers.name}, dated {today}.

Contact: {col:customers.contact}. Region: {col:customers.region}. Sales tax rate: {col:customers.tax_rate}. Terms: payment within {col:customers.terms_days} days. Credit limit: {col:customers.credit_limit}.
Your tier is {col:customers.tier}. The discount agreed is {col:customers.discount_pct} and the discount of the tier is {col:customers.tier_discount}. The tier check shows: {col:customers.tier_check}.
The minimum order of your tier is {col:customers.min_order}. Goods are sold in full cases. Prices are before sales tax and are valid until the next price notice.
Please check the attached price list and tell us of any difference before you order.
Margin report for one product and channel

Costs per unit: landed cost {col:margins.landed}, channel fees {col:margins.fees}, packaging {col:margins.pack}, pick and pack {col:margins.pick}, shipping allowance {col:margins.ship}, return allowance {col:margins.ret}.

The margin is {col:margins.margin} per unit, which is {col:margins.margin_pct} of the price. The target is {col:margins.target} and the floor is {col:margins.floor_pct}. Verdict: {col:margins.verdict}.
The price for the target margin is {col:margins.target_price} and the price for the floor margin is {col:margins.floor_price}.
Price change notice to wholesale accounts

Dear customer, from {col:pricehist.date} the price of {col:pricehist.product} (SKU {col:pricehist.sku}) changes from {col:pricehist.old_price} to {col:pricehist.new_price}, a change of {col:pricehist.change_pct}.
The reason is: {col:pricehist.reason}. Orders confirmed before this date keep the old price.
Please update your own price list and tell us if you have questions about the change.
Landed cost statement for a first order
Product: {col:launch.product}. Supplier: {col:launch.supplier}. First order: {col:launch.first_qty} units at {col:launch.unit_cost} each, goods {col:launch.goods}.
Freight: {col:launch.freight}. Duty: {col:launch.duty}. Landed total: {col:launch.landed_total}, which is {col:launch.landed_unit} per unit.
The web margin reached is {col:launch.web_margin} against a target of {col:launch.target_margin}. Check: {col:launch.meets}.
Price of the bundle: {col:bundles.bundle_price}. The items at normal prices cost {col:bundles.list_price}, so the customer saves {col:bundles.saving_pct}.

Component cost is {col:bundles.cost} and channel fees are {col:bundles.fees}. The margin is {col:bundles.margin}, which is {col:bundles.margin_pct}. Verdict: {col:bundles.verdict}. On sale from {col:bundles.on_sale_from}.
Launch brief for a new product
First order: {col:launch.first_qty} units. Landed cost per unit: {col:launch.landed_unit}. Target margin: {col:launch.target_margin}. Web margin reached: {col:launch.web_margin}.
The review is due on {col:launch.review_on}. Review status: {col:launch.review_state}. Photos, text, prices on every channel and stock must be ready before the launch date.
Channel fee comparison on an example order
Channel: {col:feerules.channel}. Fee rule: {col:feerules.fee}. Rate: {col:feerules.rate}. Fixed amount: {col:feerules.amount}. Days: {col:feerules.days}.
On an example order of {col:feerules.order_value} this rule costs {col:feerules.example}, which is {col:feerules.share} of the order.
Category: {col:targets.category}. Channel group: {col:targets.grp}. Target margin: {col:targets.target}. Floor margin: {col:targets.floor}. Last reviewed: {col:targets.reviewed}.
The average margin now is {col:targets.avg_margin}, a gap of {col:targets.gap} against the target. Verdict: {col:targets.state}. Products in the category: {col:targets.n_products}.

Open Start and type your shop name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target margin, floor margin, packaging and picking cost, items in an order and the days that count as recent.
List your suppliers on Suppliers with their freight and duty rates, then your products on Products with unit cost, weight and the five channel prices. Landed cost fills in.
Check Channel Fees. One row for each channel and fee rule: commission, payment fee, fixed fee, payout days and shipping charge.
Fill Packaging and Handling, Carriers, Shipping Allowance and Return Allowance. They feed the costs of every margin.
Read Margin by Channel. Each SKU and channel shows the margin, a verdict and the price needed for the target and the floor.
Set Target Margins by category and channel group, then read the verdict of each one.
Record every supplier rise on Cost Changes and every price move on Price History. Cost Changes shows whether prices followed.
Use Price Requests, Price Tests, Competitor Prices, Bundles, Promo Price Plan, Wholesale Tiers, Customers and Launch Plan for the pricing decisions of the year.
Use the 14 calculators for landed cost, price, order margin, floor price, cost rise, discount depth, tax, bundles, markup, shipping, returns, wholesale price, free shipping and what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Pricing Dashboard and Charts every week: margins, under-floor lines, cost rises, price changes and competitor gaps.
Know what is on hand, what to reorder and what has stopped selling
Stock levels, reorder points, counts and dead stock for an online shop
the reorder point comes from sales, lead time and safety days, with a suggested order in whole packs, its cost and the date each product runs out
Days of cover against a seasonal target
every product shows days of cover against the target of its category for this month, and the units above target become overstock value
units in the racks, the pick zone and the seconds shelf with a capacity warning for each location
receipts, sales, return restocks, transfers, write-offs and count corrections with value, and the days a receipt waited before booking
every counted line shows the difference, its value and whether it needs a recount before the system is corrected
planned counts by category and counter show days to go and, once done, the accuracy and variance from the count lines
Dead and slow stock with a clearance plan
days since the last sale, value tied up, a dead or slow class, an action and the loss at the clearance price
each stockout shows days out, its cause and the sales lost, so late suppliers and late orders can be told apart
purchase order lines still on the way show days to arrival and a late or arriving soon check for the warehouse
closing units and value for each month with write-offs and the change since last month, ready for the bookkeeper
units in each pick bin against the bin size show which bins to fill before the next picking run
Seasonal cover plan and gap cost
the days of cover you want for each category and month turn into units short and the money needed to close the gap

Stock by product: on hand, on order and days of cover
One row for each of the 40 products; on hand, on order, days of cover, cover target, overstock, stock value and the stock status fill in by themselves.
Stock by location: each product in each location
One row for each product in each location with the units there; value, the fill of the location and a capacity warning fill in by themselves.
Stock ledger: every movement of units in and out
A sample of about 400 movements (receipts, sales, return restocks, transfers, adjustments, write-offs and count corrections); value and the booking delay of a receipt fill in by themselves.
Reorder rules and suggestions: what to order this week
One row for each product with its safety days; the reorder point from sales and lead time, the order quantity in packs, the cost, the run-out date and a review warning fill in by themselves.
Open purchase orders: lines still to arrive
One row for each purchase order line that has not arrived; value, days to arrival and a late or arriving soon warning fill in by themselves.
Stock takes: counted against the system, line by line
One row for each counted product and location; the variance, its value, the share and a recount warning fill in by themselves.
Count schedule: cycle counts by category and date
One row for each planned count with its counter; the days to go, the status check, and for done counts the lines, accuracy and variance fill in from Stock Takes.
Adjustments and write-offs: units taken out or corrected
One row for each write-off, adjustment or count correction with its reason and approver; value and loss fill in by themselves.
Dead and slow stock: days since the last sale and what to do
One row for each product with its last sale and a planned discount; days since sale, value, the dead or slow class, the action and the loss at the clearance price fill in by themselves.
Stock value by month: month-end value per category
One row for each category and month with the closing units, value and write-offs; the share of the month, value per unit and the change since last month fill in by themselves.
Stockout log: days a product could not be sold
One row for each stockout with its start, end and cause; days out, lost units and lost sales fill in by themselves.
Pick zone top-ups: transfers from the main warehouse
One row for each transfer of units to the pick zone with who moved it; cartons, weight and value fill in by themselves.
Locations and storage areas with their capacity
One row for each storage area of the three locations with its capacity and lead; units in the location, its capacity and how full it is fill in by themselves.
Bin map: where each product lives in the racks
One row for each product with its rack, pick bin and bin size; units in the pick bin, the fill and a top-up warning fill in by themselves.
Seasonal cover plan: wanted cover by category and month
One row for each category and month with the days of cover you want; units needed at today's sales, units short and the money to buy them fill in by themselves.
Seconds stock: graded units on the seconds shelf
One row for each batch of second-quality units with its grade, defect and planned price; supplier, value, planned value and age fill in by themselves.
Supplier returns: units sent back with the credit expected
One row for each batch sent back to a supplier with its credit status; supplier phone, credit expected, age and a credit overdue warning fill in by themselves.
Sell-through: units sold against units available
One row for each category and month with the opening units, units received and sold and the top-ups; the share of available stock sold fills in by itself.
Products: the catalogue with cost, weight and status
One row for each of the 40 products; weight in kilograms, units on hand, days of cover and the stock status fill in from Stock by Product.
Suppliers: contact, lead time and what to order from each
One row for each of the 12 suppliers with lead time, minimum order and past lateness; the suggested order, the minimum check and open units fill in by themselves.

Warehouse lead: top up the pick zone
Hello {moved_by}, please top up the pick zone with {qty} units of {product}. Transfer {transfer_id}. Tell me when it is done.
Hello, the stock take of {category} in {location} is on {date}. Counter: {counter}. Please free the area and stop goods movements during the count.
Hello {counted_by}, please count {product} again at {location}. The system shows {system_qty} and you counted {counted_qty}, a difference of {variance}.
Hello {lead}, {area} in {location} is {use_pct} full. Please move slow stock out or tell me where space can be found.
Hello {receiver}, {product} ({qty} units, order {po_id}) arrives on {expected_date}. Please free the bays and plan the receiving.
